chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best women of my community are the most beautiful-faced and the least in dowry.'

key_terms.أَصْبَحُهُنَّ وَجْهاً: The most beautiful-faced — the superlative form indicating the brightest and most radiant face
key_terms.أُمَّتِي: My community — refers to the Islamic community (ummah) as a collective
key_terms.مَهْر: Mahr/dowry — the obligatory gift given by the groom to the bride at marriage, a right of the wife in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the best women in his community regarding beauty and dowry?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain ending at Imam al-Sadiq (AS) back to the Prophet (SAWW), describes the ideal qualities of a Muslim woman according to the Prophet: natural beauty of face combined with a modest dowry. The emphasis on a small dowry (mahr) reflects the Islamic concern for facilitating marriage, as excessive dowry demands were a known social barrier. The Prophet's teaching here encourages women and families to value accessibility in marriage over financial display.
